What to do: Document audience, geography/language, seed keywords, competing URLs, and current visibility before coding.
Done when: Audience, market/language, competitor URLs, and baseline visibility are written down.
Tools: Search; Ahrefs/Semrush or manual SERP review; competitor sites
Review cadence: Once before build; refresh at 90 days
Notes: Important strategy input, but not a universal cutover blocker.

What to do: Map each planned page to one primary intent: informational, commercial, or transactional. Do this before routes are coded.
Done when: Every planned URL has a primary query/theme, intent, and conversion goal.
Tools: Keyword research tools; Search Console later
Review cadence: Once before build; update when adding pages
Notes: Was too late in original. This decides which pages must exist.

Task: Information architecture, URL inventory and indexability matrix
What to do: List every planned URL and URL pattern before routes are coded. Record template, intent, parent links, expected status, index/noindex, canonical target, sitemap inclusion, locale and launch criticality.
Done when: A reviewable URL-pattern matrix exists and every priority URL has one internally consistent indexation plan.
Review cadence: Update whenever a page type is added
Notes: v4: expanded into the single source of truth used by crawl and launch QA.

What to do: Define the primary conversion, supporting events, reporting owner, analytics choice and success measures before instrumentation is built.
Done when: Events are named and owners know what success is.

What to do: Fix the exact brand name, legal entity, logo, and the official profiles you will claim (LinkedIn, GitHub, Crunchbase, industry directories, relevant marketplaces). These become the sameAs set in Organization schema and the basis for entity recognition.
Done when: Brand name spelling is consistent everywhere; profile URL list exists and feeds Organization schema.
Notes: New. Entity consistency is what search and AI systems use to attribute claims to you.

Applies to: Sites deciding how their content is used by AI search and training systems
Task: AI crawler, AI-feature and training policy
What to do: If the business needs an explicit policy, decide separately for Google Search crawl, index and preview controls; any Search Console generative-AI control shown for an eligible verified property; Google-Extended; OAI-SearchBot; GPTBot; and other currently documented agents. Google describes its UK Search Console control as a test and rollout to a subset of website owners while it engages with the CMA. It is not a universal AI opt-out, does not replace robots or meta directives, and is separate from Google-Extended and third-party crawler controls. Treat search/retrieval and training agents as different controls.
Done when: The optional policy records each control or agent, purpose, allow/block/limit decision, business reason, affected property or path, evidence, source URL and review date; no control is represented as broader than its documented scope.
Tools: Search Console Settings > Search generative AI; robots.txt; CDN/WAF rules; Sources sheet
Review cadence: Before launch if applicable; review quarterly
Notes: v4.4: narrowed the UK Search Console wording and separated search controls, Google-Extended and third-party crawlers. llms.txt is optional publisher metadata, not an access-control standard; Google Search says it ignores llms.txt, so using one neither helps nor harms Google Search visibility or rankings. See Sources: Google AI features, Google generative-AI optimization, OpenAI crawlers and OpenAI publisher guidance.

Task: International market, localization and URL strategy
What to do: Research intent per locale; choose folders, subdomains or ccTLDs; define localized ownership, self-canonicals, hreflang coverage and a user-controlled language switcher. Do not force users or crawlers through IP or browser-language redirects.
Done when: Each launch locale has demand evidence, an owner, URL plan, canonical/hreflang plan and localized conversion requirements.
Notes: v4: moved from the final conditional section into discovery. See Sources: international sites.

Applies to: Migration / redesign / domain or URL change
Task: Migration inventory, mapping, change freeze and rollback plan
What to do: Inventory old URLs, traffic, rankings and links; map old URLs to equivalent new content; define content parity, redirect rules, DNS timing, change freeze, backups, rollback triggers and owners. Plan to retain redirects for at least one year and keep every old domain and relevant host variant registered, secured and redirecting. For a domain or subdomain move, plan Search Console verification and Change of Address for every applicable source property variant; it supplements rather than replaces URL redirects.
Done when: The complete old-to-new map, baseline, freeze window, rollback decision, redirect-retention owner, old-domain continuity plan and applicable Search Console property/Change of Address matrix are approved before build completion.
Notes: v4.3: explicitly retains old domains/hostnames while migration redirects are required. See Sources: Google site moves.

Task: Legal, privacy, consent and accessibility scope decision
What to do: Document jurisdictions, business model, audience, data collection, required legal/consumer pages, consent approach and applicable accessibility obligations or exemptions. Assign qualified review where needed.
Done when: A dated scope decision names the applicable requirements, evidence, owners and adviser/escalation path; it is not treated as legal sign-off by the SEO team.
Review cadence: Before design/build; revisit when scope changes
Notes: New in v4. See Sources: EAA and WCAG.

What to do: Choose rendering that reliably exposes title, canonical, robots, primary heading, main content and internal links to crawlers. SSR/SSG is usually safest, but the testable output matters more than the framework.
Done when: Raw and rendered HTML on every indexable template contain equivalent critical metadata, copy and crawlable links without user interaction.
Notes: SSR or SSG. Outcome matters more than framework name.

What to do: Use real a href links, semantic landmarks, one clear primary page heading and a logical heading hierarchy. Do not treat a strict single-H1 rule as a ranking requirement.
Done when: Priority URLs are reachable through normal links; landmarks, link purpose and heading hierarchy are usable by crawlers and assistive technology.

What to do: Pick one host and slash policy. Use stable, descriptive, human-readable URL paths; prefer lowercase and hyphens, and avoid unnecessary parameters or opaque identifiers where practical. Self-canonicalize indexable pages. 301 HTTP, host, case and slash variants to the preferred URL.
Done when: Only one canonical version returns 200; alternates 301; canonical returns 200; priority URLs follow the documented descriptive path convention without accidental parameter duplicates.
Notes: v4.3: adds explicit descriptive URL and parameter conventions. See Sources: URL structure.

What to do: Return real 200, 301, 404 and, when intentionally used, 410 responses. Avoid soft 404s, redirect chains and loops; keep the 404 experience useful while returning status 404. For internal search, noindex valid result-state pages unless deliberately included in the indexability plan; return a genuine 404 for nonexistent or error-like URLs, and do not expose empty or thin search-result URLs as indexable 200 pages.
Done when: Representative success, redirect, missing, removed and internal-search URLs return the intended status and indexability; no tested empty-result or error-like URL is an indexable thin 200 or soft 404.
Notes: v3: absorbed the 404 UX requirement that was previously bundled into 1.8.

Task: Lab performance budgets and LCP strategy
What to do: Set per-template lab budgets for LCP, CLS, TBT, HTML/CSS/JS/image/font weight, request count and TTFB. Identify the likely LCP element; never lazy-load it, and use preload or fetch priority only when testing shows a benefit. Treat 75th-percentile field CWV as post-launch evidence, not a CI result.
Done when: Every launch template passes agreed lab budgets on representative mobile conditions and the LCP resource is discoverable and prioritized without harming other critical work.
Tools: Lighthouse CI; WebPageTest; PageSpeed Insights; bundle analyzer
Notes: v4: separates lab budgets from rolling field data. See Sources: Core Web Vitals.

What to do: Serve production only over valid HTTPS and permanently redirect HTTP and non-preferred host variants to the single canonical host without chains.
Done when: Certificates are valid; no mixed content exists; every tested host/protocol variant reaches one HTTPS URL in one hop.

Task: Infrastructure, security headers and third-party script budget
What to do: Use appropriate HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, caching, compression and security headers. Inventory analytics, chat, testing and advertising scripts; delay or remove noncritical code that harms interaction latency.
Done when: Infrastructure is secure and cacheable; third-party owners and performance budgets are documented; no critical journey is blocked.
Notes: v4: split from the universal HTTPS launch gate.

What to do: Password-protect or IP-restrict staging and preview environments. Use environment-conditional robots/meta controls as defense in depth and automated tests to ensure staging noindex rules cannot ship to production.
Done when: No staging or preview host is indexable; production robots.txt allows crawl and no production template emits noindex.
Tools: Host auth/basic auth; env vars; robots.txt; meta robots; Search Console
Notes: v3: narrowed to environment protection. A staging noindex leaking to production is the single most common launch catastrophe — 1.10 guards it in CI.

Applies to: Sites with meaningful images or video
What to do: Compress media, generate responsive sizes, set dimensions or aspect-ratio, use modern formats, lazy-load only below-fold media and provide captions/transcripts or alternatives where required.
Done when: Representative templates serve appropriately sized media without layout shift; the LCP asset is not lazy-loaded; accessibility alternatives are present.
Notes: v4: conditional launch gate when media ships.

Task: Critical SEO regression guards in CI
What to do: Fail production builds that emit unintended noindex, block search crawlers, omit or contradict canonicals on priority templates, or break critical internal links. Run on every pull request.
Done when: Deliberate noindex, canonical and critical-link defects fail CI and prevent merge.
Tools: Lighthouse CI / Unlighthouse; Playwright or Vitest assertions; GitHub Actions
Notes: v4: the narrow catastrophic-failure guard remains a launch gate.

What to do: Add broader checks for duplicate or missing metadata, heading quality, all internal links, schema validation, asset budgets and accessibility regressions without blocking releases on noisy rules until thresholds are proven.
Done when: Rules have owners, low false-positive rates and documented severity; high-confidence failures can be promoted to launch gates later.
Tools: Lighthouse CI; crawler; Playwright; axe; test runner

What to do: Define which filter combinations deserve indexable landing pages; control crawl paths, internal links, canonicals and noindex for the rest. Do not use robots.txt as a canonicalization or deindexing substitute.
Done when: Useful filter pages are indexable and linked; low-value combinations are absent from sitemaps and do not create uncontrolled crawl spaces.
Notes: v4: promoted to a conditional launch gate.

What to do: Provide crawlable server-rendered page URLs and normal links beneath any load-more or infinite-scroll interface. Self-canonicalize pages unless a different consolidation strategy is demonstrably correct.
Done when: Page 2+ is reachable without interaction or JavaScript and important items are discoverable through stable paginated URLs.
Notes: v4: promoted to a conditional launch gate.

What to do: Use distinct URLs per locale, correct HTML lang, self-canonicals, reciprocal hreflang including self-references, supported language-region codes and x-default only when a genuine fallback exists. Keep locale switching user controlled.
Done when: Every launch locale is crawlable and independently indexable; canonical and hreflang clusters are consistent and no forced geo redirect hides variants.
Notes: New implementation row in v4. See Sources: international sites.

Task: Product URL, variant and lifecycle architecture
What to do: Choose one stable canonical rule per product and variant; keep useful out-of-stock URLs available; define discontinued-product handling, categories, filters, pagination and internal links before catalogue routes ship.
Done when: Variant URLs do not create uncontrolled duplicates; product states have intentional status, canonical, sitemap and internal-link rules.

Applies to: Sites publishing indexable PDFs or other non-HTML files
What to do: Decide which PDFs and other files may index. Use HTTP X-Robots-Tag or Link canonical headers where HTML meta tags are unavailable, and ensure blocked indexing directives remain crawlable so bots can read them.
Done when: Every important non-HTML pattern has the intended status, X-Robots-Tag, canonical and linking behavior verified from response headers.
Review cadence: Before file templates or downloads ship
Notes: New in v4. See Sources: robots meta and canonicalization.

What to do: Define backups, deployment owner, rollback mechanism, cutover window, DNS/CDN dependencies and measurable rollback triggers for indexability, availability and conversions.
Done when: A named owner can restore the prior known-good release and content/data state within the agreed recovery time.
Review cadence: Before launch; test after platform changes

Task: Domain registration, ownership and renewal continuity
What to do: Record the registrar, registrant/organization owner, renewal method, expiry date, recovery contacts and privileged access. Enable auto-renew where appropriate, registrar/transfer lock, MFA and monitored billing/recovery paths. For migrations, keep old domains under control for at least as long as redirects are retained.
Done when: Production and any migration-source domains have a named owner, working recovery path, protected registrar access and no near-term expiry/renewal risk; old-domain retention matches the migration plan.
Tools: Registrar account; password manager; domain monitoring
Review cadence: Before launch; verify quarterly and before migrations
Notes: New in v4.3. Domain expiry is a continuity failure that DNS/SSL monitoring cannot prevent.

Applies to: Sites running A/B tests, personalization or experiments
Task: SEO-safe testing, personalization and alternate experiences
What to do: Design experiments so users and crawlers are not intentionally shown deceptive content. For alternate test URLs, use a canonical to the original when appropriate; use temporary redirects for short-lived redirect tests; keep core content and crawl paths available; end experiments when the decision is made rather than leaving variants indefinitely.
Done when: Experiment routing, canonicals/redirects and crawl behavior are documented; no cloaking pattern or permanent duplicate variant is created; test retirement has an owner/date.
Tools: Experiment platform; browser/curl; crawler; Search Console
Review cadence: Before each experiment; remove after decision
Notes: New in v4.3. Conditional guidance for experimentation-heavy sites. See Sources: website testing.

What to do: Generate sitemaps containing canonical, indexable, 200-only absolute URLs. Use lastmod only for meaningful content changes. Reference sitemaps in robots.txt; keep controls versioned. Keep noindex URLs crawlable until the directive is processed, and control low-value search, filter and tag URLs through the indexability matrix. Exclude internal-search URLs from sitemaps; use noindex for legitimate result-state pages and a real 404 for nonexistent or error-like patterns.
Done when: robots.txt and sitemaps are valid and fetchable; sitemap URLs agree with canonicals and directives; no launch URL is accidentally blocked; low-value and empty internal-search patterns have explicit crawl, status, canonical, noindex and sitemap rules with no contradictory signals.
Notes: v4: clarifies that robots.txt is not a deindexing or canonicalization mechanism.

What to do: Give meaningful images accurate alternative text based on their purpose; give decorative images empty alt. Avoid keyword stuffing and do not duplicate adjacent captions unnecessarily.
Done when: Priority content images communicate the same purpose without sight; decorative assets are silent to assistive technology.
Notes: v4: separates accessibility-critical alt handling from low-impact filenames.

Applies to: Sites where image search, Discover or image-rich search appearance matters
What to do: Use stable descriptive filenames and relevant surrounding copy where operationally practical; consider image sitemaps for otherwise hard-to-discover assets. For pages targeting Discover or image-rich search surfaces, provide a representative high-quality image, expose the preferred image through supported page metadata where useful, and allow large image previews when the content and rights permit.
Done when: Important assets are crawlable and discoverable; priority pages have an intentional representative image; image-preview controls do not accidentally suppress eligible large previews.
Tools: CMS/media pipeline; image sitemap; page metadata; robots meta
Notes: v4.3: expanded from filenames to preferred-image and Discover/search-preview readiness. See Sources: Discover.

What to do: Verify the appropriate domain property before launch, assign durable owners, confirm the preferred production property and prepare the sitemap for submission. Do not couple Search Console verification to a particular analytics product.
Done when: At least two durable owners can access the correct production property and the planned sitemap URL is documented.
Notes: v4: separated from GTM, GA4 and Consent Mode.

Applies to: Sites using analytics or conversion measurement
What to do: Implement the chosen analytics stack and planned conversions. Prevent duplicate events; configure internal/test traffic, cross-domain and referral handling, ecommerce values where relevant, timezone, retention and ownership. When Google Analytics is used, associate the correct Search Console property with the GA property so Search performance data can be analyzed alongside site behavior.
Done when: Pageviews and real test conversions appear once with correct source, URL, consent state and value; internal/test behavior is documented and controlled; any intended Search Console ↔ Analytics association is active and owned.
Tools: Chosen analytics debugger; browser network tools; tag debugger; Search Console Associations
Review cadence: Before launch and after tracking changes
Notes: v4.3: adds Search Console ↔ Google Analytics association where GA is used. See Sources: Search Console associations.

Applies to: Sites where consent is required and/or Google tags use Consent Mode
Task: Consent platform and Google Consent Mode configuration
What to do: Implement the legally approved consent experience. If Google tags are used, set regional defaults and update analytics_storage, ad_storage, ad_user_data and ad_personalization as applicable. Consent Mode communicates choices to Google; it is not legal compliance by itself.
Done when: Before and after consent, tags and storage follow the approved policy; withdrawal works; denied-consent paths remain functional; evidence is approved by the accountable owner.
Tools: CMP; Tag Assistant; browser storage/network tools; Sources sheet
Review cadence: Before launch and after CMP/tag changes
Notes: v4: conditional and corrected. See Sources: Google Consent Mode.

Applies to: Templates eligible for useful structured data
What to do: For each template, document supported schema types, required and recommended properties, visible-content source and owner. Implement only accurate JSON-LD that reflects the page. FAQ rich results stopped appearing 7 May 2026; Search Console/Rich Results Test support was removed in June and Search Console API support is removed in August 2026. FAQPage remains a valid schema.org type, so accurate existing markup may stay, but do not build it merely for Google rich results. HowTo rich results are already deprecated.
Done when: Every marked template has valid, visible-content-backed markup and an owner; unsupported or ineligible schema is omitted.
Tools: Schema.org validator; Rich Results Test; Search Console; Sources sheet
Notes: v4.3: clarifies staged FAQ deprecation and that accurate FAQPage markup need not be stripped. See Sources.

What to do: Add og:title, og:description, og:url, og:image, and Twitter/X cards for sharing.
Done when: Social preview tools show correct title, description, and image.
Tools: Open Graph debugger; social preview tools

Applies to: Sites with an approved AI crawler policy
Task: Implement and verify optional AI crawler directives
What to do: Translate the approved 0.6 policy into robots.txt and edge controls. Verify the documented user agents actually receive the intended response; do not confuse training, search and user-triggered agents.
Done when: robots.txt, CDN/WAF behavior and a dated user-agent test agree with the policy.
Tools: robots.txt tester; curl with custom UA; Cloudflare/CDN bot dashboard; server logs
Review cadence: Launch; re-verify after any CDN change
Notes: v4: merged with the corrected policy and made optional.

What to do: Wire IndexNow into the publish/deploy pipeline so new and updated URLs are pushed to Bing, Yandex, Seznam and Naver on change. Google does not participate — it still relies on the sitemap.
Done when: Key generated on site; publishing a page triggers a successful IndexNow submission.
Notes: v4: optional optimization, not a universal launch requirement.

Task: Product structured data, merchant feed and policy configuration
What to do: For ecommerce, expose real visible product data and genuine reviews only, implement eligible Product structured data, keep price, availability, currency, identifiers, shipping and return information consistent with the page and merchant feeds, and validate representative variants. Never create ratings or reviews, mark up testimonials as product reviews when they are not, use self-serving review markup, conceal incentives, or condition an incentive on positive sentiment.
Done when: Representative products validate; rendered page, markup and feed agree; marked-up reviews are authentic, attributable and visible; any permitted incentive is disclosed and never tied to sentiment; no fabricated or self-serving review markup exists.
Tools: Rich Results Test; Merchant Center; Screaming Frog; Search Console Associations
Notes: v4.3: adds Search Console ↔ Merchant Center association. See Sources: Search Console associations.

Task: Google Business Profile and local entity setup
What to do: Claim and verify the profile; set accurate NAP, categories, service areas, hours and website URL. Use a tagged website link where measurement policy permits and keep major citations consistent.
Done when: The profile is verified, accurate and linked to the correct landing page; ownership and review-response responsibility are assigned.
Notes: v4: moved to configuration and demoted from a universal cutover blocker.

Task: Favicon, site name and search identity
What to do: Provide a stable crawlable favicon on the site hostname and define the preferred site name consistently. Use WebSite structured data on the home page where appropriate, keep Organization/brand naming aligned, and verify that robots rules do not block the home page or favicon asset.
Done when: The production home page exposes an intentional site name and favicon; the favicon is square, stable and crawlable; site-name/brand signals are consistent with the approved brand baseline.
Tools: Browser; Rich Results/schema validator; robots test; Search Console
Notes: New in v4.3. Covers two visible SERP identity elements previously absent. See Sources: favicon and site names.

Applies to: Sites where indexable video is a primary content asset
What to do: Give important videos stable crawlable watch pages with descriptive titles/context, accessible players and strong thumbnails. Implement accurate VideoObject where eligible; use a video sitemap when it materially improves discovery; keep thumbnail/video resources crawlable and monitor video indexing/search performance after launch.
Done when: Priority videos have crawlable watch pages, accessible thumbnails/player resources and accurate video metadata; eligible structured data validates; any video sitemap is fetchable and owned.
Tools: Rich Results Test; video sitemap; Search Console; crawler
Review cadence: Before launch for video templates; review when publishing video
Notes: New in v4.3. Conditional module for sites where video is an organic acquisition surface. See Sources: Video SEO.

Applies to: Sites with paywalled or registration-gated indexable content
What to do: Decide which gated pages should remain indexable and ensure Googlebot can access the same eligible content under the approved sampling model. Mark paywalled sections with supported structured data where applicable, keep preview behavior intentional, and prevent account/checkout/private-user areas from leaking into the index.
Done when: Indexable gated pages have documented sampling/access rules and valid markup where used; private/account content is not unintentionally indexable; crawler and logged-out behavior match the approved policy.
Tools: URL Inspection; Rich Results/schema validator; crawler; access-control tests
Review cadence: Before gated content launches; after access-model changes
Notes: New in v4.3. Conditional module for publisher/membership products. See Sources: paywalled content.

Applies to: News, publisher or editorial sites targeting Discover / Preferred Sources
Task: Publisher Discover and Preferred Sources readiness
What to do: For eligible publisher/editorial sites, review Discover presentation requirements, representative-image quality and metadata, and whether the site is eligible for Google's Preferred Sources experience. If strategically useful, implement the supported Preferred Sources prompt/button without making it a ranking claim or launch dependency.
Done when: Publisher pages use intentional representative images and eligible metadata; Preferred Sources eligibility/implementation has a dated decision; no unsupported promise about ranking impact is made.
Tools: Search Central docs; page metadata; Search Console
Notes: New in v4.3. Optional publisher discovery module. See Sources: Discover and Preferred Sources.

Applies to: Sites with hierarchical content or category structures
What to do: Provide visible, crawlable breadcrumb navigation that represents a typical user path and helps people move through the hierarchy. Keep linked ancestors aligned with canonical URLs. Add accurate BreadcrumbList markup only when the visible hierarchy exists; do not merely mirror URL strings or invent a hierarchy in structured data.
Done when: Priority hierarchical templates show a usable breadcrumb trail; linked ancestors return 200 and use the intended canonicals; BreadcrumbList matches the visible navigation and passes validation on representative pages.
Tools: Rich Results Test; crawler; accessibility QA; Sources sheet
Review cadence: Before launch for hierarchical templates; after navigation changes
Notes: New in v4.4. Conditional, non-gate enhancement for hierarchical sites. See Sources: Breadcrumb navigation.

What to do: Write unique, accurate titles and clear primary headings for priority URLs. Match the page intent and avoid arbitrary character-count rules or keyword repetition.
Done when: Every priority URL has an accurate, distinct title and primary heading; no title or heading is empty, misleading or duplicated by template error.
Notes: v4: meta descriptions split into a separate P1 row.

What to do: Write accurate, useful descriptions for priority pages. Accept that search engines may rewrite snippets; prioritize clarity and conversion value over fixed length.
Done when: Priority pages have non-misleading descriptions and no systemic blank or duplicated template output.

What to do: Link related pages using descriptive anchors when it naturally benefits the reader. Ensure priority pages are reachable in few clicks.
Done when: Priority pages reachable in few clicks; no important orphans; natural anchor text.
Notes: Replaces forced 'topic clusters' with natural contextual linking.

Task: Trust, contact and required legal/consumer pages
What to do: Publish accurate About and contact information plus the privacy, terms, company, returns, accessibility or consumer-information pages required by the approved 0.9 scope. Add real authors and sources where responsibility matters.
Done when: Required pages are accurate, accessible, owned and linked from appropriate locations; claims have accountable people or organizations.

Task: Helpful structured answers, not GEO tricks
What to do: Write original pages answering real queries with specifics, limits, pricing/process, and first-hand detail.
Done when: Priority pages answer the query clearly; claims are supportable; no AI bait.
Notes: v3: pair with 3.9 for the format side of the same principle.

Applies to: YMYL, regulated, product or consequential factual claims
Task: Editorial evidence, fact-check and approval trail
What to do: Record primary sources, reviewer, approval date, material limitations and next review date for consequential claims. Use qualified legal, medical, financial or technical review when the subject requires it.
Done when: Launch claims are supportable and current; evidence and approvals are findable; unsupported testimonials, comparisons or guarantees are removed.
Review cadence: Before publish; at expiry or material change

What to do: Define and finish the smallest set of priority landing, trust and conversion pages needed for the launch proposition. Do not block launch on an aspirational long-term editorial calendar.
Done when: Every URL marked launch-critical in the inventory has complete, approved copy, media, metadata, links and conversion path.

Task: Post-launch content production plan and cadence
What to do: Turn the keyword and intent map into a sustainable dated backlog with owners, review steps and publication dates after the minimum launch set is complete.
Done when: The next content tranche has named owners, realistic dates and an accountable backlog owner.
Notes: v4: demoted; the actual launch content set is covered by 3.7.

What to do: Structure priority pages so a machine and a hurried human can extract a correct, attributable answer: descriptive subheadings, direct answers near the relevant question, specific figures and cited sources where claims need support. For editorial, informational or consequential content where readers reasonably expect authorship or freshness signals, show an accurate author/reviewer and meaningful publish/update dates. Do not force bylines or dates onto transactional landing pages merely for SEO.
Done when: Priority content answers its main query clearly; claims that need support carry sources and context; authorship and dates appear where readers would reasonably expect them rather than as site-wide boilerplate.
Tools: Editorial review; GSC Generative AI report later
Notes: v4.3: narrows byline/date requirements to content where readers reasonably expect authorship or freshness. See Sources: helpful content.

What to do: Before publishing, confirm no existing page already targets the same intent. If one does, strengthen it or merge instead of adding a near-duplicate.
Done when: Each publish has a recorded decision: new page, or update/merge of an existing URL.
Tools: site: search; GSC query/page report; internal URL inventory
Notes: New. Cheaper to prevent than to untangle in the 7.2 decay audit.

Task: Accessible content, links and media QA
What to do: Check heading meaning, descriptive link text, plain language where appropriate, table headers, image alternatives, captions/transcripts, page language and instructions that do not depend only on color, shape or position.
Done when: Priority content remains understandable and operable with images, sound or styling unavailable; media alternatives are accurate.
Tools: Editorial accessibility checklist; screen reader sampling

What to do: Localize intent, terminology, currency, units, legal information, shipping/service availability, contacts and conversion copy. Do not publish raw machine translation without accountable review.
Done when: Each launch locale is reviewed by a qualified human and matches the local query, offer, legal scope and conversion journey.
Tools: Locale briefs; human QA; URL inventory

Applies to: Sites allowing public UGC, marketplace listings, partner pages or other third-party content
Task: UGC, marketplace and third-party content governance
What to do: Define moderation, spam prevention, publishing thresholds and indexation rules for user/partner content before it can create large crawlable sections. Qualify paid/advertising links with sponsored and user-generated links with ugc where appropriate. Prevent scaled low-value pages, parasitic third-party publishing and unmanaged profile/listing spam from becoming an indexable acquisition strategy. For ratings and reviews, prohibit fabricated submissions, undisclosed incentives and incentives conditioned on positive sentiment; define disclosure, moderation and takedown evidence.
Done when: Moderation and escalation owners exist; low-value/spam UGC cannot create uncontrolled indexable inventory; paid and UGC links are qualified where required; third-party publishing rules align with search spam policies. Review records show provenance, moderation decisions and any required incentive disclosure.
Tools: Moderation tools; crawler; Search Console; spam policy review
Notes: New in v4.3. Conditional launch gate for public/third-party content surfaces. See Sources: spam policies and outbound-link qualification.

Task: Full staging crawl: raw HTML and rendered output
What to do: Crawl the release candidate before launch with raw-HTML and JavaScript rendering modes for status codes, titles, headings, canonicals, directives, links, assets and orphan detection. Production crawling is a separate launch-day row.
Done when: No unexplained critical difference exists between raw and rendered output; priority URLs have no broken links, missing metadata or indexation conflicts.
Review cadence: Before launch and after big releases
Notes: v4: split staging QA from the production crawl.

What to do: Compare the crawl against the 0.3 matrix for expected status, index directive, canonical, sitemap inclusion, internal links, locale and launch criticality. Resolve every mismatch explicitly.
Done when: Every launch URL pattern matches the approved matrix; exceptions have an owner, reason and launch decision.

Task: Mobile, forms, cookie and critical-journey QA
What to do: Test priority templates and conversion journeys on real phones and keyboards. Check forms, validation, labels, focus, contrast, tap targets, zoom, navigation and cookie interactions; avoid intrusive interstitials.
Done when: Mobile forms work; banner does not permanently block content; usable controls.
Notes: Good accessibility overlaps with good SEO.

Applies to: All sites; conformance target follows the 0.9 scope
Task: Automated and manual accessibility conformance QA
What to do: Test representative templates with automated tools and human evaluation: keyboard-only operation, visible focus, screen-reader sampling, accessible names, reflow/zoom, form errors, landmarks, dialogs, motion, captions and critical status messages.
Done when: No critical barrier blocks content or conversion; applicable conformance evidence, known exceptions, owners and remediation dates are documented.
Tools: axe; Lighthouse; keyboard; screen reader; WCAG checklist; Sources sheet
Review cadence: Before launch and after critical UI changes
Notes: New in v4. Automated tools alone cannot establish conformance. See Sources: WCAG and evaluation.

What to do: Run the agreed lab profile on the homepage and every major template. Inspect the actual LCP resource, render-blocking work, layout shifts, long tasks and third-party code; compare with the 1.5 budget.
Done when: Every launch template passes the approved lab budget or has a signed exception with user impact, owner and remediation date.
Tools: Lighthouse CI; WebPageTest; browser performance panel

What to do: Validate every marked template in both Schema.org Validator and any relevant rich-result test. Compare names, offers, availability, ratings, dates and authors with visible content and source data.
Done when: No relevant errors or misleading mismatches remain; required and recommended properties have documented decisions.
Notes: v4: conditional launch gate when schema is actually shipped.

Applies to: Sites using analytics, conversion tags or consent controls
Task: Analytics, conversion and consent QA matrix
What to do: Test pageviews and conversions across consent granted, denied, withdrawn, direct, organic, campaign, cross-domain and error paths. Check duplicates, values, source attribution, storage and console/network errors.
Done when: A dated matrix proves expected behavior for each applicable state and journey; defects have owners and retest evidence.
Tools: Analytics debugger; Tag Assistant; network/storage tools

Applies to: Migration / redesign / domain or URL change
Task: Migration redirect, content-parity and rollback rehearsal
What to do: Test the complete redirect map before cutover, including query/host variants and high-value backlinks. Compare old and new content, metadata, canonicals, internal links, sitemaps and structured data; rehearse rollback.
Done when: High-value and sampled long-tail URLs resolve to relevant equivalents without chains; parity gaps are signed off; rollback succeeds in a controlled test.
Tools: Old/new crawl diff; redirect tester; analytics/GSC baseline

What to do: Crawl every launch locale for status, self-canonical, language, reciprocal hreflang, fallback, localized links and accidental redirects. Verify locale content and conversion parity.
Done when: Hreflang clusters are complete and reciprocal; locales are indexable, localized and reachable without forced routing.
Tools: Crawler; hreflang validator; locale QA matrix

Task: Product, checkout, variant, feed and policy QA
What to do: Test product states, variants, categories, filters, cart/checkout, price/currency, availability, shipping, returns, structured data and Merchant Center feed parity on representative products.
Done when: No duplicate variant trap, price/feed mismatch, orphan product, broken checkout or misleading product markup remains.
Tools: Crawler; Rich Results Test; Merchant Center; checkout test
Review cadence: Before launch and catalogue platform changes

Task: Dated pre-launch crawl, performance and visibility baseline
What to do: Archive a dated baseline before go-live: full crawl export, CWV field/lab numbers, schema validation output, and (if replacing a live site) current rankings, traffic and top landing pages. Store it with the project.
Done when: Dated export set is stored and findable; anyone can compare post-launch numbers against it.
Tools: Screaming Frog export; PageSpeed; GSC export; analytics export
Notes: v4: P1 for new sites; migration-critical baseline evidence is required in 0.8 and 4.8.

What to do: Confirm backups are current, the previous release is restorable, credentials and owners are available, and rollback thresholds for availability, indexability and conversions are measurable during the launch window.
Done when: A timed rehearsal or equivalent proof demonstrates restoration within the recovery target; launch contacts and escalation order are current.

Task: DNS cutover and production smoke test
What to do: After cutover, verify DNS, certificates, preferred host, homepage and priority statuses, robots.txt, sitemap, canonicals, forms, critical journeys, assets and availability on the public hostname.
Done when: The production smoke checklist is signed off during the launch window and monitoring shows no critical availability or indexability defect.
Notes: v4: migration redirects moved to their own conditional row.

Applies to: Migration / redesign / domain or URL change
Task: Migration redirects live before traffic cutover
What to do: Deploy and verify the approved redirect map before switching traffic. Recheck priority and sampled long-tail old URLs, chains, canonicals, internal links, new sitemap and any required change-of-address workflow. For domain or subdomain moves, submit and verify Change of Address for every applicable source property variant after redirects are live.
Done when: Old URLs resolve immediately to relevant new equivalents; no critical chain, loop, mass-homepage redirect or missing high-value mapping exists. Applicable domain-variant properties show completed Change of Address steps and remain verified for monitoring.
Notes: v3: priority normalised to P0; the condition lives in "Applies to".

What to do: Crawl the public site after launch and reconcile status, robots, canonicals, metadata, internal links, sitemap URLs and rendered content against the signed release candidate and indexability matrix.
Done when: No critical production-only difference or blocked priority URL remains; exceptions have owners and immediate decisions.
Review cadence: Launch day and after emergency fixes

Task: Submit sitemap and inspect priority URLs
What to do: Submit the production sitemap in the already verified Search Console property. Inspect the homepage and priority templates for live response, rendered HTML, indexing permission and selected canonical.
Done when: The sitemap is accepted/readable and live inspection sees the intended canonical, directives and content on priority URLs.
Notes: v4: Search Console ownership moved earlier; Bing is a separate P1 row.

What to do: Alert on uptime, 5xx, DNS/SSL expiry, robots.txt changes, sitemap failure, canonical changes and unexpected noindex on representative priority URLs. Test alert plumbing safely in staging or with a synthetic fixture, not by breaking production.
Done when: A safe test reaches a monitored human within the target time; alert owners, severity and response steps are documented.
Tools: Uptime monitor (Better Stack, Cronitor, UptimeRobot); scheduled GitHub Action; GSC alerts
Notes: v4: adds DNS/SSL and sitemap monitoring and removes destructive production testing.

Applies to: Sites using analytics or conversion measurement
Task: Live analytics and conversion smoke test
What to do: Complete real production journeys and verify pageviews, consent state, conversion events, source attribution, value and deduplication without exposing personal or test data improperly.
Done when: Production analytics receives one accurate event per test action and rejected-consent paths remain functional.
Tools: Analytics realtime/debug view; tag debugger; transaction records

What to do: Compare production evidence with agreed availability, indexability, performance and conversion thresholds. Keep the release team available until the decision window closes; roll back when a trigger is met.
Done when: A named decision owner records GO, remediate-in-place or rollback with evidence and timestamps.

What to do: Verify the site and submit the production sitemap in Bing Webmaster Tools; confirm any IndexNow integration if adopted.
Done when: The property is owned, sitemap accepted and optional IndexNow submission recorded.

What to do: Compare submitted, crawled, canonical and indexed URLs by template; inspect homepage and priority pages; assign causes and owners for exclusions or duplicate-canonical selections.
Done when: Known blockers have owners and fixes.

What to do: Review RUM immediately where available and CrUX/Search Console once sufficient rolling field data exists. Evaluate LCP, INP and CLS at the 75th percentile by major template; keep lab testing for diagnosis.
Done when: Field regressions and segments have owners; lack of CrUX coverage is recorded rather than treated as a pass.
Notes: v4: phase-6 P0 removed and field/lab evidence separated.

What to do: Track queries, clicks, conversions, indexation, crawl errors, CWV and content gaps. Define traffic, conversion and indexed-page anomaly thresholds, reporting lag and the owner who investigates.
Done when: A weekly report and actionable alert thresholds exist; every material anomaly has a documented disposition.

Applies to: Sites with available AI-search reporting or meaningful AI referrals
What to do: Establish how the site appears in AI answers where reporting is available: use Search Console's dedicated Generative AI performance views, add an analytics segment for referrals from chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, copilot and similar, and spot-check a small set of real brand/category prompts. Treat the Search Console reports as rollout-dependent and record the earliest available reporting date rather than fabricating a pre-launch history.
Done when: A dated baseline of available AI impressions and AI referral sessions exists; reporting availability/start date is recorded; prompt spot-checks are logged.
Tools: Search Console Generative AI report; GA4 referral report; manual prompt tests
Notes: v4.3: clarifies rollout-dependent reporting and prevents invented pre-availability baselines. See Sources: Generative AI performance reports.

What to do: Check GSC Security Issues and Manual Actions, keep dependencies and CMS patched, and watch for injected spam pages via a site: query on the new domain.
Done when: No open security issues or manual actions; patching owner named.
Tools: Search Console; Dependabot/npm audit; site: query
Notes: New. A hacked new site loses trust before it ever earns any.

Applies to: Migration / redesign / domain or URL change
What to do: Monitor old high-value URLs, server 404s, redirect chains, crawl rate, indexed old/new URLs, traffic and ranking transitions. Correct missed mappings without redirecting irrelevant URLs to the homepage.
Done when: Material missed redirects and parity defects are fixed; visibility changes are explained and monitored through stabilization.
Review cadence: Daily first week; weekly through day 30

Applies to: Sites using analytics or conversion measurement
What to do: Compare analytics conversions and revenue with forms, CRM, orders or other systems of record. Investigate duplicates, missing events, attribution changes and consent-related gaps.
Done when: Material differences are quantified, explained and assigned; dashboards use documented definitions.

What to do: Watch the GSC Links report for unusual patterns on a new domain. Treat disavow as a last resort tied to a manual action or clear negative-SEO campaign — routine disavowing of ordinary spam links does more harm than good.
Done when: Link profile reviewed; no action taken unless there is a manual action or clear attack.
Notes: v3: demoted from P1 and reworded. Google ignores most spam links automatically.

What to do: Check product/feed/rich-result errors, variant canonicals, hreflang clusters, locale indexation and localized conversions using the reports relevant to the deployed features.
Done when: Errors and coverage gaps have owners, priority and retest evidence; no template-wide regression remains unexplained.
Tools: Search Console; Merchant Center; crawler; analytics

Task: Ongoing monitoring, incident ownership and response SLA
What to do: Maintain alerts for availability, robots/noindex/canonical changes, sitemap failures, organic/conversion anomalies, security issues and expiring DNS/SSL dependencies. Keep severity, owner, response time and rollback steps current.
Done when: Alert routes are tested quarterly; incidents have timestamps, owners, decisions, remediation and prevention follow-up.
Tools: Monitoring; Search Console; analytics; incident log

What to do: Review pages losing clicks, outdated facts, cannibalization, weak conversions, broken links, and thin content. Refresh/merge/prune with reason.
Done when: Dated audit log has decisions per declining URL.

What to do: Re-run the phase 4 crawl, CWV check and schema validation once a quarter and after any major release. Templates rot: new components, third-party scripts and CMS changes reintroduce old problems.
Done when: Dated quarterly crawl exists; regressions are ticketed with owners.
Tools: Screaming Frog; PageSpeed; Rich Results Test
Notes: New. Complements 7.2, which only covers content decay.

Task: Release-based SEO, accessibility and performance regression review
What to do: After major template, CMS, navigation, tracking, CDN or design-system releases, rerun the affected crawl, lab budget, structured-data, analytics and accessibility checks rather than waiting for the quarterly cycle.
Done when: Every major release links to scoped regression evidence and owned follow-up tickets.
Tools: Release checklist; CI; crawler; test tools

Task: Digital PR and legitimate link earning
What to do: Earn relevant mentions through original research, tools, expertise, partnerships, communities and legitimate press. Measure relevance, referral value and durable brand impact rather than raw link count.
Done when: An owned outreach plan and documented relevant wins exist without paid or manipulative link schemes.

Task: Off-page link, review and reputation governance
What to do: Prohibit buying or exchanging links for ranking manipulation; qualify sponsored and user-generated links appropriately. Prohibit fabricated reviews, undisclosed incentives and incentives conditioned on positive sentiment; document how legitimate review requests, disclosures, moderation and takedowns work. Monitor material reviews, unlinked brand mentions, profile/citation accuracy and escalation paths for genuine reputation issues.
Done when: A written policy, owner and review cadence exist; outreach and partnerships comply with search-engine spam policies; review provenance and moderation are auditable; permitted incentives are disclosed and never tied to sentiment.
Tools: Brand monitoring; review platforms; link reports

What to do: Sample new and high-traffic templates with automated and manual checks; review keyboard, screen-reader, zoom/reflow, forms, dialogs, media alternatives and content patterns. Track remediation by severity.
Done when: Dated samples and issue trends exist; critical barriers trigger immediate incident handling.
Tools: axe; keyboard; screen reader; WCAG checklist
Review cadence: Quarterly and after major UI changes

What to do: Audit Googlebot hits and wasted crawl on large or filter-heavy sites. Skip for small launch unless needed.
Done when: Can identify Googlebot fetches, waste, and response errors.
Review cadence: Monthly or when crawl is broken

Applies to: Sites using structured data, internationalization or merchant feeds
What to do: Monitor template errors, eligibility changes, visible-content mismatches, hreflang coverage and feed/page discrepancies. Revalidate after schema, locale, CMS or catalogue changes.
Done when: Current reports show no unexplained template-wide defect; retired or unsupported markup is removed deliberately.
Tools: Search Console; validators; Merchant Center; crawler

Task: Security, manual actions and dependency maintenance
What to do: Monitor Search Console Security Issues and Manual Actions, patch dependencies and CMS components, scan for injected pages and review privileged access. Coordinate security incidents with indexation and reputation response.
Done when: No unowned critical vulnerability, security issue or manual action remains; patching and access-review cadence is documented.
Tools: Search Console; dependency scanning; site query; access logs
